Quick answer: Yoga for arthritis can reduce joint pain by 22% and improve physical function by 20%, according to a 2019 review of 17 studies. Gentle poses like Mountain Pose, Cat-Cow, and Seated Twist improve posture, spinal mobility, and reduce stiffness. Always use props, avoid pushing through pain, and warm up gently before practising for 15-20 minutes daily.

Yoga for Arthritis: Gentle, Evidence-Based Relief

Yoga combines gentle stretching, strengthening, and mindfulness — making it one of the most holistic approaches to arthritis management. NICE recognises yoga as a beneficial activity for people with chronic pain.

What the Research Shows

A 2019 systematic review of 17 studies found yoga:

  • Reduced joint pain by 22% (moderate evidence)
  • Improved physical function by 20%
  • Decreased stiffness by 18%
  • Enhanced mental wellbeing and reduced depression
  • Was safe with no serious adverse events reported

8 Gentle Yoga Poses for Arthritis

1. Mountain Pose (Tadasana)

Stand tall, feet hip-width apart. Ground through your feet, lengthen your spine. Hold 30 seconds. Benefits: Improves posture and body awareness

2. Cat-Cow Stretch

On hands and knees, alternate between arching (cow) and rounding (cat) your spine. Benefits: Mobilises the entire spine, reduces stiffness

3. Warrior II (Modified)

Wide stance, front knee bent (not past ankle), arms extended. Use a chair if needed. Benefits: Strengthens legs, opens hips

4. Seated Twist

Sit tall in a chair. Place your right hand on your left knee, gently twist left. Hold 15 seconds each side. Benefits: Spinal mobility, reduces back stiffness

5. Bridge Pose

Lie on your back, knees bent. Slowly lift hips, hold 10 seconds. Lower slowly. Benefits: Strengthens glutes and core, supports hip and knee joints

6. Child's Pose

Kneel, sit back on heels (use a cushion if needed), extend arms forward. Benefits: Gentle back stretch, calming

7. Legs Up the Wall

Lie on your back with legs resting up a wall. Relax for 3–5 minutes. Benefits: Reduces swelling in legs and feet, deeply relaxing

8. Corpse Pose (Savasana)

Lie flat, arms by sides, eyes closed. Focus on breathing for 5 minutes. Benefits: Activates parasympathetic nervous system, reduces pain perception

Yoga Tips for Arthritis

  • Use props freely — blocks, straps, blankets, and bolsters reduce strain
  • Chair yoga is excellent if getting to the floor is difficult
  • Never push through pain — modify or skip any pose that causes sharp pain
  • Warm up first — gentle joint circles before poses
  • Practice regularly — 15–20 minutes daily is better than one long session

Finding the Right Class

  • Look for "gentle yoga", "restorative yoga", or "yoga for arthritis" classes
  • Many studios and NHS physiotherapy departments offer adapted classes
  • Online options: Yoga with Adriene (free YouTube), Versus Arthritis yoga videos

Written by Anna Stevens, Yoga Therapist and HCPC Registered Physiotherapist

Practical next steps for Yoga for Arthritis: Gentle Poses That Help

If you came here about Yoga for Arthritis: Gentle Poses That Help, pick one change you can keep for a fortnight rather than overhauling everything at once. Note what hurts, what helps, and what you have already tried, then take that list to your GP, rheumatology nurse or physiotherapist so the conversation stays concrete.

In many areas you can ask your NHS trust about self-referral to physiotherapy or lifestyle support without waiting for a hospital letter. Check your GP surgery website or the NHS App for the route that applies where you live.

Pacing on good and bad days

On better days it is tempting to catch up on everything at once. Spread chores and exercise across the week instead. Use the two-hour rule many physiotherapists suggest: if pain or fatigue is clearly worse two hours after activity, the dose was too high — trim the next session rather than stopping altogether.

Peer support etiquette

Share what helps you without prescribing it for others. Conditions, medicines and life circumstances differ. If someone is in crisis, encourage them toward NHS 111, their GP, or emergency services rather than relying on a forum alone.

Quick questions about Yoga Arthritis Gentle Poses

Is this a substitute for seeing a clinician? No. Use it to prepare questions and understand options, then confirm decisions with your NHS team.

How long before I judge whether a change helped? Give most habit or exercise changes at least two to four weeks, unless pain or swelling clearly worsens — in that case scale back sooner.

What should I track? Joint pain (0–10), morning stiffness time, sleep quality, and how far you can walk or how long you can type or stand. Patterns beat one-off ratings.

Safety and when to get urgent help

This page is general information for people in the United Kingdom, not personal medical advice. Seek urgent help via NHS 111 or A&E if you have sudden inability to move a joint, hot swollen joint with fever, chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or symptoms that feel immediately dangerous.

Keep learning with us

Explore related guides on Living With Arthritis UK — try the guides hub, diet hub, exercise hub, or site search to filter by topic and length. If benefits or work questions are on your mind, start at the Benefits & PIP hub.

Keep expectations kind while you work on yoga for arthritis: gentle poses that help. Arthritis symptoms fluctuate; a quieter week does not mean you imagined earlier pain, and a flare does not mean every helpful habit has failed. Adjust one variable at a time so you can see what truly helps.
